title: The Sour milk in the cup
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：sour　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sour 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1983 the athlete wrote of ① a sour milk in the cup in the programme, and everybody in the stadium said at once that it was ② sourer than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the athlete, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the sour ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the sourest milk in the cup anybody in the stadium had ever seen, or so the programme for September 1977 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too sour to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the trainer who had come to help; the sour ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the bib at the far track, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a sour look of the old man, and said that no trainer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as sour as the look of the old man they had once had in the old stadium. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was sour or not, and he said so.

By 1990 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the programme. What the line asked for was ⑦ something sour, and nothing besides. The trainer from the next stadium called the whole plan ⑧ quite sour; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the programme kept the names of the sour ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1993, in silence, she wrote of another sour milk in the cup in the same programme, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ sourer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The sourest look of the old man in the whole stadium, she said in 1995, was the one she could never quite name; the sour ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 发酸（前置定语 a sour milk in the cup：1983 年运动员在秩序册里记下的那件发酸的牛奶）
B. adj. 发酸／乖戾（比较级 sourer than：文中两处，一处比杯里发酸的牛奶，一处比预想）
C. adj. 发酸／乖戾（最高级 the sourest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 发酸（表语 too sour to do：母亲觉得它太发酸，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 乖戾（前置定语 a sour look of the old man：叔叔把整件事称作一桩乖戾的神色）
F. adj. 乖戾（同级比较 as sour as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩老人乖戾的神色相比）
G. adj. 乖戾（后置定语 something sour：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 乖戾（受程度副词修饰 quite sour：那位陪练的评价）

items.q: a sour milk in the cup
the sourest milk in the cup anybody
a sour look of the old man
The sourest look of the old man in

answers.why: sour 意为“发酸”，1983 年运动员在秩序册里记下的是“一件发酸的牛奶”，此处作前置定语 a sour milk in the cup。
sour 意为“发酸”，此处用比较级 sourer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
sour 意为“发酸”，秩序册上 九月 那行字说它是体育场里最发酸的一件，故用最高级 the sourest milk in the cup。
sour 意为“发酸”，母亲认为这件东西“太发酸了，谁也用不上”，too sour to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
sour 意为“乖戾”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩乖戾的神色”，此处作前置定语 a sour look of the old man。
sour 意为“乖戾”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩老人乖戾的神色一样乖戾”，同级比较用 as sour as。
sour 意为“乖戾”，秩序册上那半行字要的是“乖戾的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something sour。
sour 意为“乖戾”，邻体育场来的那位陪练认为这套计划“相当乖戾”，quite 修饰原级 sour。
sour 意为“乖戾”，1993 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要乖戾”，故用比较级 sourer than。
sour 意为“乖戾”，母亲 1995 年说的是“整个体育场里最乖戾的那一桩”，故用最高级 the sourest look of the old man。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1983 年，运动员在秩序册里记下了一件发酸的牛奶。（a sour milk in the cup）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更发酸。（sourer than …）
母亲觉得它太发酸，谁也用不上。（too sour to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩乖戾的神色。（a sour look of the old man）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩老人乖戾的神色一样乖戾。（as sour as …）
到了 1990 年，秩序册上只剩半行字：要的是一件乖戾的东西。（something sour）
answers: In 1983 the athlete wrote of a sour milk in the cup in the programme.
Everybody said it was sourer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too sour to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a sour look of the old man.
He said nobody would call it as sour as the look of the old man they had once had.
By 1990 the programme asked for nothing but something sour.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 sour 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1983 the athlete wrote of a sour milk in the cup in the programme, and nobody forgot it.
It was the sourest milk in the cup in the stadium, or so the programme says.
My mother thought it too sour to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a sour look of the old man, and nobody argued with him.
The trainer from the next stadium called the plan quite sour, and everybody laughed.
The sour ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
